attests: point-in-time reads of wrapped totalSupply and origin-chain escrow balance at the pinned blocks named in each record; a ratio, not a rate, not a grade, not a reserve attestation, not a certificate

states.ESCROW_PARITY_READ: both reads succeeded at the pinned blocks; a read, not a measurement (the card doctrine reserves MEASURED for graded banks and refuses it on point-in-time cards)
states.UNCHECKABLE_NATIVE_ISSUANCE: natively issued on the destination chain; no escrow exists; supply read, no ratio claimed
states.INDEXED_CUSTODIAL: reserve held by a custodian off-chain or on another ledger; supply read; no reserve readable from here; no ratio claimed
states.UNMEASURED: a read failed; error recorded; nothing inferred

terms_boundary: Public RPC endpoints, no API key. Endpoint substitutions are recorded per read.

rows.name: GBTD — Great British Tokenised Deposits (UK Finance industry pilot)
rows.operator: UK Finance (industry pilot with participating banks)
rows.status_as_documented: Pilot phase described as running "until mid-2026". That stated end date has passed as of 2026-09-14; the current status is UNVERIFIED.
rows.what_as_documented: "GBTD" is defined by UK Finance as Great British Tokenised Deposits — a digital representation of sterling commercial bank money. Participants listed: Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds Banking Group, Monzo, NatWest, Nationwide, Santander; supported by Quant, EY and Linklaters. Use cases: marketplace person-to-person payments, remortgaging, digital asset settlement.
rows.on_chain_observable: NO — no public contract or ledger is published on the page.

rows.name: Project Agorá
rows.operator: BIS Innovation Hub with the Institute of International Finance (convenors)
rows.status_as_documented: Experimental. The 2026-05-27 BIS release says the prototype showed tokenisation can address inefficiencies in wholesale cross-border payments and that work will advance to real-value testing; no production timeline is given.
rows.what_as_documented: A shared programmable platform with tokenised central bank reserves and tokenised commercial bank deposits. Central banks: Bank of England, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Bank of France, Bank of Japan, Bank of Korea, Bank of Mexico, Swiss National Bank; more than 40 private-sector institutions; Bank of Canada joining.
rows.on_chain_observable: NO — research prototype; no public ledger.
